title: Cold & Flu Relief

drivers.name: Store closure (Monday)
drivers.evidence: Store closed Monday; 1/7 of week lost. Historical sales show ~14% drop in comparable partial-week scenarios.

drivers.name: Price increase (6.2%)
drivers.evidence: Previous price hike to $12.03 (2026-09-28) caused a 30% drop vs baseline. However, later week (2026-10-05) at same price showed 30% uplift. Noise-adjusted estimate shrinks effect to -10%.

adjustment.analysis: The baseline median is 18.5. The target week has a 6.2% price increase to $12.03, which is above regular price. Historical data shows price increases reduce demand: the last price hike (2026-09-28) saw sales drop to 13 (vs baseline 18.5), a 30% decline. The same price point in 2026-10-05 saw 24 units (30% above baseline), suggesting the price increase may not have a consistent negative effect. However, the store closure on Monday (a full day lost) likely reduces sales by ~14% (1/7 of weekly sales). No event or promotion is planned. The classical uplift model suggests no effect, but that ignores the price increase and closure. Evidence is moderate: one past price hike with a clear drop, but the closure is unique. Adjust downward by ~14% for closure, and ~10% for price (shrunk due to mixed signals). Combined effect shrinks toward 1.0 due to thin evidence.

brief:
PRODUCT: Cold & Flu Relief | category Health | Store #12 (Austin, TX)
TARGET WEEK: 2026-11-30 to 2026-12-06 (8 weeks after the last week with sales data)

KNOWN PLAN FOR THE TARGET WEEK:
  events: none
  shelf price: 12.03 (+6.2% vs regular price 11.33)
  planner notes: Store closed Monday for renovation

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 18.5 | 5%-95%: 1.4 - 40.9 | 10%-90%: 5.8 - 35.9

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-46% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
